record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.original_question: In the Ekpyrotic and cyclic scenarios in M-theory, is the Milne state globally asymptotically stable when the higher-order terms enter the evolution dominantly rather than subdominantly, and what does that reveal about ekpyrosis and the broader structure of M-theory cosmology?

evidence.quote:
4.6 Ekpyrosis and the Milne state with asymptotically dominant higher-order terms
This is a continuation of the previous problem concerning the asymptotic global stability of the Milne state in the Ekpyrotic and cyclic scenarios in M-theory. However, this time one is interested in the eﬀects of the higher-order terms now entering dominantly in the evolution.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the low-energy effective action of M-theory compactified to four dimensions in the setting of Ekpyrotic and cyclic cosmological scenarios. In these scenarios one studies spatially homogeneous (e.g. Bianchi-type) cosmological evolutions, with a contracting phase governed by a scalar field with steep negative exponential potential coupled to gravity together with quadratic and higher-order curvature corrections (e.g. Gauss–Bonnet and other α'- and loop-corrections appearing in heterotic M-theory). The Milne state is the spatially flat (or hyperbolic) self-similar vacuum solution with linearly expanding/contracting scale factor a(t) ∝ |t| and vanishing Weyl curvature, regarded as a fixed point of the cosmological dynamical system.

Previous analysis of these scenarios treats the higher-order curvature terms as subdominant perturbations of the two-derivative Einstein–scalar evolution and asks for global asymptotic stability of the Milne state under such perturbations. The problem here is the complementary regime: assume the higher-order terms enter the evolution equations dominantly, i.e. they are not treated as small corrections to the Einstein–scalar dynamics but instead control the leading asymptotic behaviour.

Question: In this dominant higher-order regime of Ekpyrotic and cyclic M-theory cosmology, is the Milne state globally asymptotically stable as a solution of the resulting cosmological evolution equations on the space of homogeneous initial data? Provide a rigorous proof or disproof of global asymptotic stability, and determine the implications of the answer for the viability of ekpyrosis and for the asymptotic structure of M-theory cosmology.
artifact.category_tag: string cosmology and Milne state stability
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches turn up related but distinct results: nonlinear stability of the Milne model has been established for Einstein–Vlasov and certain non-minimal scalar–tensor settings, and ekpyrotic scenarios are known to have stability-friendly features. However, no source addresses the specific question of global asymptotic stability of the Milne state in Ekpyrotic/cyclic M-theory cosmology when higher-order curvature corrections enter dominantly rather than subdominantly. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Nonlinear Stability of the Milne Model with Matter
status_evidence.snippet: First stability result for the Milne model in presence of matter (Einstein–Vlasov), showing 3+1-dimensional Milne model is future nonlinearly asymptotically stable.
status_evidence.claim: Stability of Milne is known in adjacent matter models but not in the dominant higher-order M-theory regime.

status_evidence.title: Inflation vs. Ekpyrosis — Comparing stability in general non-minimal theory
status_evidence.snippet: Ekpyrosis ensures stability in non-minimal theories under various equations of state.
status_evidence.claim: Related stability questions for ekpyrosis are studied, but not the specific dominant higher-order Milne regime.

status_evidence.title: Ekpyrotic and Cyclic Cosmology (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Review of ekpyrotic/cyclic scenarios in M-theory; higher-order corrections discussed.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reviews treat higher-order terms perturbatively, leaving the dominant regime open.
